name: Dangerous Sandbox Configuration
description: A setting explicitly disables or bypasses sandbox restrictions.
why: Unrestricted execution can expose files and system resources to actions initiated during Codex work.
recommendation: Use the narrowest supported sandbox mode and review any required exceptions.

name: No-Prompt Approval Policy
description: The approval policy is set to never prompt; this is a heuristic warning whose impact depends on the effective sandbox.
why: A no-prompt policy changes how approval requests are handled, while sandbox restrictions still affect command access. CodexGuard cannot determine the effective runtime policy from this file alone.
recommendation: Confirm that unattended operation is intentional and review the effective sandbox mode; choose an interactive policy if user prompts are required.

name: Suspicious MCP Configuration
description: An MCP command uses a shell or inline execution pattern that merits review.
why: Shell wrappers and inline code can obscure the behavior and provenance of an MCP process.
recommendation: Verify the server source and command, pin trusted versions, and avoid shell evaluation.

name: CODEX_HOME Redirection
description: A CODEX_HOME environment-variable assignment was found in an environment example.
why: Changing the configuration home can change which Codex settings and trust boundaries apply.
recommendation: Confirm the environment override is intentional and points to a trusted, controlled directory.

name: Potential Secret Exposure
description: A value matches a common credential or private-key pattern.
why: Credentials in project files can be copied, committed, or exposed to tools and collaborators.
recommendation: Remove the credential, rotate it if real, and use a secure secret-management mechanism.

name: Hook Requires Manual Review
description: A hook is configured. Its presence alone is not evidence of unsafe behavior.
why: Hooks can run commands in response to Codex events, so their source, scope, and trigger deserve review.
recommendation: Review the configured hook and its effects; retain it if it is trusted and needed.

name: Suspicious Project Instructions
description: Project guidance contains language associated with instruction override or unsafe execution.
why: Untrusted repository instructions may attempt to influence tool behavior or disclose sensitive data.
recommendation: Review the instruction in context and remove unsafe or unrelated directives.
